title: Beautiful in one’s own eyes
odia:
ନବ ଗୁଞ୍ଜର
ଆପଣା ମନକୁ ଆପେ ସୁନ୍ଦର।
literal_meaning: Navagunjara—to one’s own mind, oneself is beautiful.
meaning_odia: ନବ ଗୁଞ୍ଜର ନାମ ପରେ ନିଜ ମନକୁ ନିଜେ ସୁନ୍ଦର ଲାଗିବାର କଥା ଆସିଛି। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠରେ ଏହା ନିଜ ପ୍ରତି ଥିବା ଅନୁକୂଳ ବିଚାରକୁ ନେଇ ଏକ ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ। ଏଥିରୁ ନବଗୁଞ୍ଜରଙ୍କୁ ଅସୁନ୍ଦର କୁହାଯାଇଛି ବୋଲି ଧରାଯାଇନାହିଁ; ମୂଳରେ ସେପରି ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନା ନାହିଁ।
explanation: The judgement of beauty is located inside the person doing the judging. Our editorial reading notices how readily self-regard supplies its own favourable verdict. The opening names Navagunjara, but the line gives no description that would justify declaring the figure ugly.
usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone admires their own appearance and assumes everyone must agree. A friend gently recalls the saying about being beautiful in one’s own eyes.
cultural_context: The named figure in the short first line is followed by the rhyming ସୁନ୍ଦର. Repeated self-reference in ଆପଣା and ଆପେ makes the second line turn back on its own judge; no surrounding story is supplied.

witnesses.locator: Page26, two-line item beginning ନବ ଗୁଞ୍ଜର, after the bowed-person/punch couplet.

english_summary: One’s own judgement readily finds oneself beautiful.
